cohort: The study included 9,096,788 pregnant women who delivered or had a maternal death, of whom 2127 were diagnosed with peripartum cardiomyopathy.
finding: Women diagnosed with peripartum cardiomyopathy experienced significantly higher rates of adverse maternal, delivery, and neonatal outcomes compared to those without PPCM.
mod_finding: Women with PPCM had significantly higher rates of caesarean delivery.
